content: We further define two dense vectors $X_u$ and $Y_i$. We call $X_u$ the “latent factors for character $u$", and $Y_i$ the “latent factors for HLA $i$". The dot product of these two vectors produces a value ($X_u^TY_i$) that approximates $P_{u,i}$ (see Figure FIGREF9). This is analogous to factoring the matrix $P$ into two separate matrices, where one contains the latent factors for characters, and the other contains the latent factors for HLAs. We find that $X_u$ and $Y_i$ being 36-dimensional produces decent results. To bring $X_u^TY_i$ as close as possible to $P_{u,i}$, we minimize the following loss function using the Conjugate Gradient Method BIBREF30:
